column1: # Maps each tests/test_*.sh suite to the paths it exercises, so
# .github/workflows/shell-tests.yml can select only the tests relevant to a
# PR's changed files. Built by reading each test's header comment and the
# guessed) — see the PR description for the audit.
#   test    - path to the test file, relative to repo root
#   globs   - semicolon-separated list of path globs this test exercises
#             (always includes the test's own path). A changed file matching
#             ANY of these globs makes this test "relevant" for the PR.
#   status  - "run" (executed in CI) or "skip-ci" (never run in CI)
#   reason  - required when status=skip-ci; empty for status=run
# A PR that changes .github/workflows/shell-tests.yml or this map file runs
# ALL status=run tests, regardless of the glob match (see the workflow).
# Scope note: this map covers only the top-level tests/test_*.sh suites
# test_*.sh, and every tests/test_*.R / tests/testthat/** suite are out of
# scope for this PR (R suites are a follow-up; the two sh files under
# tests/hooks/ and tests/codex_fallback/ were not part of the requested
# glob and are not audited here).

confirmed via two real CI runs (JohnGavin/llm#1279, both "23 passed, 1 failed"): the test's own precondition self-check asserts `gh` is NOT found under PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, true on the author's Homebrew Mac but false on ubuntu-latest, which ships gh at /usr/bin/gh — not fixable via a CI shim without removing gh from the runner's own PATH
